info.bio: Aunque Concrete Blonde surgió en Los Ángeles en 1982 (como Dream 6), el grupo no publicó ningún LP hasta 1987. Su insistente control creativo les creó problemas con muchas discográficas, pero I.R.S. asumió el riesgo publicando su debut homónimo, que sonó demasiado a The Pretenders. Dos años más tarde, "Free" se reveló como un trabajo más sólido donde brilló la composición de Johnette Napolitano. El álbum produjo el éxito para adolescentes

scenes.name: Roots-rock de los ochenta y cow-punk
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Como en 1970 tras 1966, la new wave de 1976 va seguida de un revival del roots-rock, esta vez gradual y disfrazado: punks que desfiguran los estilos tradicionales (X, Dream Syndicate, Gun Club) y los «cow-punks» que tocan country ambientado entre inadaptados: Long Ryders, Jason & The Scorchers, Fetchin Bones, Lone Justice, Beat Farmers. El populismo de Los Lobos, Del Fuegos, Del-Lords y Walkabouts; en la Costa Oeste, los dementes Camper Van Beethoven, Donner Party, Catheads, Thin White Rope y los American Music Club de Mark Eitzel; en Texas, Wild Seeds, Poi Dog Pondering, Glass Eye; en los Grandes Lagos, BoDeans, Soul Asylum, Afghan Whigs, Shrimp Boat y los canadienses Cowboy Junkies. Nashville se renueva con los neotradicionalistas (George Strait, Randy Travis, Garth Brooks, Lyle Lovett, Steve Earle, Dwight Yoakam) y el surf instrumental vuelve con Shadowy Men On A Shadowy Planet.

podcast.title: Chris Sangerides as Producer
podcast.body: The Tragically Hip expressed strong admiration for the sound of Concrete Blonde's records. This appreciation for Concrete Blonde's sound, which producer Chris Sangerides had worked on, was a key factor in The Hip's decision to collaborate with him for *Fully Completely*, even though they were initially unaware of his broader reputation in heavy metal. "We love the sound of those records. We really didn't know of his involvement as the godfather of English, heavy metal or whatever."

xref.title: Chris Sangerides as Producer for Fully Completely
xref.body: Chris Sangerides, a Greek Cypriot, was chosen to produce *Fully Completely*. He was known for his work with heavy metal acts like Judas Priest, Black Sabbath, Ozzy, and Thin Lizzy, but The Tragically Hip were primarily drawn to the sound of records he produced for Concrete Blonde. The band felt disarmed by his lovely demeanor, and he showed his enthusiasm by traveling to Toronto to see them play at the Horseshoe Tavern before recording. Sangerides implemented a traditional 1970s recording technique, which was "completely alien" to the band's usual live-style approach, focusing on building tracks from the bass and drums upwards. "In my recollection, it was our idea to work with Chris, but in retrospect, I think Bruce Dickinson was very good at putting an idea out there and making you think that it was your own."

xref.title: Producer for The Tragically Hip's Fully Completely
xref.body: Chris Sangerides, a Greek Cypriot, produced The Tragically Hip's *Fully Completely*. He was known for working with heavy metal bands such as Judas Priest, Black Sabbath, Ozzy, and Thin Lizzy, but The Hip were specifically impressed by his work with Concrete Blonde. Sangerides was enthusiastic about producing *Fully Completely*, traveling to Toronto to see the band perform live before committing. He introduced a "traditional 1970s recording" approach, which was initially "completely alien" to The Hip, by stripping everything down and building tracks from the bass and drums up over three weeks, which resulted in a bigger, more isolated sound. "Chris really wanted to strip everything down in a way that I think is much more traditional 1970s recording, but for us it was completely alien."
